summary: Every SPEC item is implemented as specified. ranges.ts adds TYPICAL_VPIP/typicalVpip (77.5/24/16.5) and renames relativePfrPct to relativeStatPct, keeping the old name as an alias (A-1). It maps open-raise/three-bet/four-bet to relative-pfr and limp/call-raise/call-three-bet to relative-vpip, leaves check unscaled, and computes o = min(100, d x stat / typical) for every scaled line. The 30-hand threshold, the blend (scaledWidthPct), resizeRange and the default range files are unchanged; the only logic change is the o expression. The new acceptance tests would fail under the old raw rule: PFR 18 would give 18, not 34.54; heads-up VPIP 77.5 would give 77.5, not 11.76; full-ring VPIP 33 would give 33, not 55.2. Using the wrong table size's typical value would also fail them (full ring with 24 gives 37.95), and the cap is asserted with toBe(100) and the all-classes start. The locked re-pins change only the listed assertions and names: observed-ranges AC#2, observed-resize AC#1/2/3 (narrow target), observed-reraise AC#4/5 and the AC#6 row, small-table AC#1, and review-numbers 34.4%/33.7%. The golden JSON changes only the a6s stats (100/12/9) and the justification. The protected untouched files have an empty diff. The targeted vitest run passed (16 files, 354 passed, 1 pre-existing slow skip). The signoff says MATCH. Recorded deviation (the docs cap sentence names the BTN open-raise): I recomputed every default width, and the cap thresholds 52.1/53.8/57.9 (6-max) and 45.8/44.7/59.8 (full ring) are exactly the three lowest per size, so the sentence is accurate and better than the spec wording. One NIT on a ragged doc line wrap.
